confidence_scale.A: High: official administrative or census data with published methodology; near-complete coverage
confidence_scale.B: Medium-high: research organization or probability survey with stated n, dates and method
confidence_scale.C: Medium: vendor or member survey with stated n and method but self-selected or non-representative frame
confidence_scale.D: Low-medium: vendor operational data or member census with no stated n, or unreconciled internal inconsistencies
confidence_scale.E: Low: self-selected small survey, key content gated or unverified

sources.requested_name: U.S. Census 2023 County Business Patterns, NAICS 23
sources.title: 2023 County Business Patterns (CBP)
sources.release_note: Tip sheet CB24-TPS.46 '2023 County Business Patterns Now Available', Thu June 26, 2025
sources.data_period: Employment in pay period including March 12, 2023; establishments with paid employees any time in 2023
sources.sample_definition: Universe of U.S. establishments with paid employees (Business Register); excludes self-employed individuals and businesses with an EIN but no employees. 2017 NAICS.
sources.methodology: Administrative records (payroll tax filings) plus Census surveys; noise infusion for disclosure avoidance. Size classes by mid-March paid employment. 'Paid employment' includes salaried officers of corporations; excludes sole proprietors and partners of unincorporated businesses (glossary). The '<5' class includes establishments with no paid employees in mid-March that paid wages at some time in the year.
sources.how_verified: Bulk file cbp23us.zip and cbp23st.zip downloaded in-browser from www2.census.gov and parsed; glossary read directly. Census API was not usable (now requires a key).
sources.limitations: Establishment, not firm; employee count excludes unincorporated owners but includes incorporated owner-officers; data are 2023.

sources.title: 2024 Nonemployer Statistics (NES)
sources.release_note: Tip sheet CB26-TPS.59 'Census Bureau Releases 2024 Nonemployer Statistics', Tue Sept 29, 2026 (no news release or headline numbers)
sources.sample_definition: Businesses with no paid employees, subject to federal income tax, receipts of $1,000 or more ($1 or more for Construction). 2022 NAICS.
sources.methodology: IRS administrative records (business income tax returns). Excludes government and nonprofits. Primary nonsampling error is improper inclusion of employer establishments. Census advises against time-series use. Geography by mailing address.
sources.unit_of_count: Nonemployer establishment (generally one business tax return)
sources.how_verified: Bulk files downloaded in-browser from www2.census.gov and parsed; tip sheet, methodology and NAICS code list read.
sources.limitations: Includes side and part-time businesses (construction threshold is $1); construction detail stops at 4- or 5-digit NAICS, so no individual counts for roofing, painting, siding, concrete, drywall.

sources.authors: Amber B. Trueblood, Derek Dufoe, Raina D. Brooks, William Harris
sources.publisher: CPWR - The Center for Construction Research and Training (NIOSH cooperative agreement OH 012761)
sources.data_period: CBP 2014-2023, NES 2014-2023, CFOI 2011-2022, SOII 2024, QCEW 2024, Dodge/CPWR survey 2025
